security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and Mermaid syntax examples. One npx rendering command and two mermaid.live links are real low-to-medium risks because they involve external tooling or third-party preview.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx command for Mermaid rendering.
remediation.suggestion: Pin @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli to a trusted version and tell users to review packages before running npx.
Warn users not to paste confidential diagrams into third-party preview sites. Recommend local rendering for sensitive work.

remediation.issue: The rendering command uses automatic yes behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid -y in marketplace guidance or explain that it skips interactive package confirmation.

content.value_statement: Mermaid diagrams often render poorly in GitHub Markdown. This skill gives clear styling rules, syntax patterns, and review steps for readable diagrams.
actual_capabilities: Explains GitHub-compatible Mermaid syntax and styling patterns.
Provides a reusable classDef and subgraph template.
Shows color pairings for light and dark GitHub themes.
Identifies common Mermaid mistakes before publishing.
Recommends rendering and visual review before committing diagrams.
limitations: Does not validate Mermaid syntax automatically.
Focuses on GitHub Markdown rendering behavior.
Does not create image assets by itself.
Includes an optional command that requires local tool trust.

use_cases.title: Document Pull Request Architecture
use_cases.description: Create readable flowcharts for design changes in GitHub pull requests.

use_cases.title: Standardize Technical Documentation
use_cases.description: Apply consistent Mermaid styling across README files and project guides.

use_cases.title: Clarify Process Flows
use_cases.description: Turn process descriptions into diagrams that remain readable in dark and light themes.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Simple Flowchart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub-ready Mermaid flowchart for this process. Use dark fills, light strokes, rounded nodes, and clear labels.

prompt_templates.title: Improve An Existing Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Mermaid diagram for GitHub rendering. Fix syntax, labels, colors, subgraphs, and line routing issues.

prompt_templates.title: Design An Architecture Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid architecture diagram for these components. Group related services, keep arrows short, and use transparent subgraphs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Diagram Readability
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this rendered Mermaid diagram as a reader. Identify crossings, unclear starts, disconnected groups, and styling problems.

output_examples.input: A request moves from user input through validation, processing, and success or retry paths.
output_examples.output: A GitHub-ready flowchart with rounded nodes, a decision point, and dark-mode compatible styling.

output_examples.input: A Mermaid diagram has colored subgraph fills, unquoted labels, and labels with escaped line breaks.
output_examples.output: A revised diagram plan using transparent subgraphs, quoted labels, and browser-compatible line breaks.

output_examples.input: A system has frontend, API, worker, database, and monitoring components.
output_examples.output: An architecture diagram layout that groups services and keeps the primary request path easy to trace.

best_practices: Preview every diagram before committing it to documentation.
Use dark fills, light strokes, and white text for nodes.
Keep primary flows clear and move extra detail into prose.
anti_patterns: Using Font Awesome icons in GitHub Mermaid diagrams.
Using light node fills that fail in dark mode.
Creating dense diagrams with many crossing secondary edges.

faq.question: Does this skill generate Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides prompts and rules for creating Mermaid diagrams that render well in GitHub Markdown.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is text-based and works with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it avoid Font Awesome icons?
faq.answer: GitHub Mermaid rendering does not support those icons, so they appear as plain text.

faq.question: Why are dark fills recommended?
faq.answer: Dark fills with light strokes keep nodes readable in both GitHub light and dark themes.

faq.question: Can it validate Mermaid syntax automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends rendering and review, but it does not include an automatic validator.

faq.question: Should sensitive diagrams use mermaid.live?
faq.answer: No. Use local rendering for confidential diagrams to avoid sending design details to a third-party site.
